answer: Each agent gets one reward-bearing identity only after proving control of a unique, scarce resource, such as a bonded stake locked for a fixed period. The protocol caps voting and payout weight by that bond, then slashes it when an identity is caught duplicating claims or violating rules. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital for every extra identity and risks losing it; copying names is not enough. A dune of quartz under a zephyr is cheaper than that.
